about: Bad-faith flags (S1). `POST /api/flags` scores when the flagged dealer message was bad faith and costs points when it was not. The flag rule is deterministic (agents/inspector.py: the structured offer binds a lesser item than the thread asked for, AND the words claim the better one); Jev only decides whether the evidence justifies switching GUARDRAILS.md allow_flags on. A yes never sends a flag by itself: a human sets allow_flags and the desk sends at most max_flags_per_process, never to a trusted dealer.

instructions.question: Should we switch bad-faith flags on now, given the flag rule replayed over the captured feed: `dealer_offers_inspected`, `clean`, `blocked`, `would_flag_untrusted_dealers`, `would_flag_trusted_dealers`, `untrusted_dealers_seen` and `untrusted_dealer_offers`?
instructions.note: Trusted dealers (`trusted_dealers`, Abuela and Chato) are honest by construction and never flagged: a would-flag on them is a false positive of the rule. The rule targets the L4 'Tricksters', who slip a lesser card into the structured offer while the words name a good one. Each correct flag scores and each wrong one costs; at most `max_flags_per_process` flags are sent per process.

criteria.true: The rule has fired on untrusted dealers' offers (`would_flag_untrusted_dealers` > 0) and never on the trusted dealers' many honest offers (`would_flag_trusted_dealers` = 0 over hundreds of offers), so a flag would most likely be correct.
criteria.false: No untrusted dealer has been seen or none of its offers would be flagged (nothing to gain yet), or the rule fired on a trusted dealer's honest offer (it is not precise enough), or the sample is too small to trust.
